liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Cream Puff War** (2 reviews): Cream Puff War is described as a set closer that blew the reviewer away; Cream Puff War is the only highlight of the show for this reviewer [8][12]
- **Hey Little One** (2 reviews): Singles out Hey Little One as powerful, with Jerry's early wailing guitar sounding pretty good; Praises Jerry's crooning vocal on Hey Little One [3][4]
- **Viola Lee Blues** (1 review): Viola Lee Blues is not the best version heard, but has an unmistakable quality; Phil's intro is loved [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **Standing On The Corner**: rare: 6 archived performances [15]
- **You Don't Have To Ask**: rare: 7 archived performances [15]
- **Stealin'**: rare: 14 archived performances [15]
- **Cardboard Cowboy**: rare: 4 archived performances [15]
- **Cream Puff War**: rare: 12 archived performances [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1966-07-30.sbd.GEMS.94631.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 13 songs; 65 min; rated 3.4/5 by 10 [1]. Said about its sound: Calls this upgrade very clear for a recording made 42 years earlier; Reviewer regards the acoustic quality of this recording as outstanding among Grateful Dead recordings [5][13]
- **gd66-07-30.sbd.vernon.9387.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 7 songs; 30 min; rated 3.17/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: Sound quality is good, but the reviewer notes much of the show is missing from this tape [3]

## Around the show

- Opens with stage banter greeting Captain Consciousness, followed by a single round of applause and a joke that their fame preceded them [8]
- Notes the audience applause is sparse on the recording [9]
- Criticizes Pigpen's flat, quivering singing and says much of the set sounds like practice [12]
- Second show of the band's first foreign booking, part of the Trips Festival at Hastings Park with a 52-projector light and film show [14]
- Reviewer believes the tape holds the whole show as one set, though it has carried various dates [14]
- The tape's date is uncertain, with two possible song lists given for it [2]
- Reviewer prefers the previous night's show, though still finds this one a treat [5]
- Recommends collectors get both the July 29 and July 30, 1966 Vancouver shows [6]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1966-07-30.sbd.GEMS.94631.flac16**: source: SBD>10" 1/2 track 15ips MR [1]. Also: This GEMS upgrade from September 2008 improves on earlier circulating copies of the show [1]
- **gd66-07-30.sbd.vernon.9387.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Raoul Duke and Matt Vernon; source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Transfer chain listed as soundboard, then MR, then unknown steps, then CDR [2]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Guitar Club Magazine: [“The Grateful Dead” tra poco compie 50 anni!](https://www.guitarclubmagazine.com/read-uen59-the-grateful-dead-tra-poco-compie-50-anni.html) [16]
